model: REIT operating profit capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; stapled property trust plus development and funds management)

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026 total OPERATING revenue by segment (Investment 626 + Funds 115 + Development 1,911 + Unallocated 2 = 2,654; FY26 AR note B segment table, MGR.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt ~line 7918). The Metrics CSV carries 2,626 (statutory IS revenue line); the operating-basis total is used so that the margin path ties to Group operating EBIT (826) on the same basis. Development revenue (1,895) is ~71% of the total and is lumpy with settlement timing, which is why the margin, not the revenue line, is the anchor.
inputs.share_count_basis: 3,945,860,217 stapled securities on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY26 AR line 11747). Diluted WANOS used for diluted EPS is 3,946m, identical to basic (line 10277): performance rights are immaterial/on-market settled, so no dilution add. Held FLAT: equity compensation is expensed inside operating profit; no buyback program (nil repurchases since FY2019).
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. The flow being capitalised is Operating profit after tax, which is already AFTER net financing costs (FY26 A$269m, including A$53m COGS interest and the A$38m JV/associate share) and operating tax. Deducting the A$3,517m balance-sheet net debt (company measure at hedged rate; borrowings 3,788 less cash 238 = 3,550 unhedged) on top would charge the debt twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never FCF/WACC on a post-interest flow, never subtract net debt afterwards). total_debt and cash below are recorded for audit only; headline gearing 24.1% (look-through 27.2%), target 20-30%, A-/A3 ratings.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026 free cash flow to equity = distributions declared for FY26 (9.5c x 3,946m = A$376m, FY26 AR 5-year table line 4250), i.e. Operating profit after tax 508 less A$132m retained and reinvested (26% retention). NOT the statutory FCF of 571 (OCF 875 less capex 304): FY26 OCF was inflated by ~A$500m of asset sales and capital-partner sell-downs (Harbourside, Kindira, SEED stage 2) flowing through operating activities, and statutory FCF for a developer-REIT swings from -796 (FY23) to +571 (FY26) on inventory and settlement timing.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Operating profit after tax, FY2026 (Mirvac's own distributable-earnings measure; FY26 AR line 7904 and reconciliation at line 8014: statutory 677 less 98 revaluation gains, 168 JV non-cash share, plus 86 lease-incentive amortisation etc.). Positive every year FY16-FY26 (482, 534, 580, 631, 602, 550, 596, 580, 552, 474, 508) while statutory NPAT was -165 (FY23) and -805 (FY24) on property devaluations. FFO is 516 (adds back 8 of SaaS costs); the more conservative operating-profit line is used.
inputs.sbc_source: Security-based payments expense (A$5m FY26 per statement of changes in equity F4, line 7649; A$9m FY25, A$7m FY24) is expensed inside operating profit and NOT added back, so no second deduction is made in the flows. It is ~1% of operating profit; house and street bases coincide (SBC-zero convention).
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest revenue A$7m (FY26) nets inside the A$269m net financing costs line and is left in the flows because no cash is added to the valuation and net debt is not deducted: the matching-asset rule is satisfied in the other direction.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-23T06:10:04Z (ASX regular close 16:00 AEST; Yahoo v8 chart meta; 52-week range 1.607-2.46)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the AUD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest and post-tax and no net debt is deducted. AUD 10-year government yield ~4.4% (Sept 2026) + 5.5% equity risk premium x beta ~0.95 = 9.6%, rounded to 9.5%. Set 0.5pp below the 10.0% used for CHC.AX/GMG.AX because ~2/3 of segment EBIT (Investment 602 of 908) is passive rent on a 98%-occupied, 5.0-year WALE portfolio and the group carries A-/A3 ratings; the development-cycle and interest-rate risk is charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked on the rate (owner-fcf.md 7f). One rate across all scenarios. At the current price the base flows imply a ~8.2% cost of equity (see required_return_table).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost: lease principal (A$6m FY26) and interest (A$3m) sit inside operating profit via the AASB 16 net-movement adjustment in the reconciliation; lease liabilities (A$44m) are immaterial and excluded from debt, which is zero in the model anyway.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are attributable-only by construction: Operating profit after tax is stated attributable to stapled securityholders, and JV/associate results enter as the Group's share of net profit. No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.tax_note: Operating income tax expense FY26 49 on operating PBT 557 (Group EBIT 826 less net financing costs 269) = 8.8%; FY25 38/512 = 7.4%. Blended because Mirvac Property Trust (passive rent) is a flow-through trust while Mirvac Limited (development, funds) pays 30%. Modelled at 9.0% flat; a higher development share of earnings pushes it up. Cash taxes paid were 30 (FY26), -26 (FY25), -25 (FY24) so cash tax runs at or below the operating charge.
inputs.engine_mapping: ebitda_margin_path = (Operating profit before tax + D&A) / operating revenue, i.e. EBITDA AFTER the A$269m net financing costs (FY26: (557+63)/2654 = 23.4%; FY25: (474+38+69)/2503 = 23.2%). da_pct_path = 63/2654 = 2.4%. cash_tax_rate_path applies to EBIT = operating profit before tax. capex_pct_path = D&A add-back (2.4%) + retained earnings reinvested (FY27: operating profit ~523 less distributions at 9.9c x 3,946 = 391 -> ~132 retained = 4.8% of revenue), so FCF out of the engine is free cash flow to equity = distributable cash after growth reinvestment. FY27 year-1 check: revenue 2,734 x 23.4% = 640 EBITDA; -66 D&A; 574 EBIT; -52 tax; 522 NOPAT = 13.2c per security, inside the 13.2-13.4c guidance range; FCFE 391 = 9.9c guided DPS.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Mirvac straddles two routing rows (an internally managed property trust holding A$7.7bn of investment properties plus A$4.0bn of JV/fund co-investments, and an operating development and funds-management business that contributed 306 of 908 segment EBIT in FY26). Rather than a sum-of-parts with a separate NTA leg, the group's own single distributable measure, Operating profit after tax, is projected and capitalised at the cost of equity with net debt held at zero (REIT-row rule), on the component engine so the dashboard reproduces it -- the same construction as CHC.AX and GMG.AX. The engine's 'EBITDA' is post-net-interest by construction (see engine_mapping). Statutory NPAT (-165 FY23, -805 FY24, +68 FY25, +677 FY26) is fair-value noise around a stable 474-631 operating profit and is not used anywhere. Statutory FCF is likewise not used (developer inventory and asset-sale timing). MID-CYCLE CHECK: FY26 operating EPS of 12.9c sits BELOW the 10-year range (FY16 13.0c, FY19 peak 17.1c, FY25 trough 12.0c) and below the 10-year average operating profit of A$553m, so no mid-cycle haircut is applied to the base; the FY27 guidance year (+3% at the 13.3c midpoint) is the anchor and the bear case carries a FY25-style trough. NTA CROSS-CHECK (memo): NTA A$2.33/security; the earnings-based values sit well below NTA because operating ROE on book equity is only 5.4% (508/9,355) against a 9.5% cost of equity -- the market's 24% discount to NTA at the current price is the same finding. A buyer paying NTA is underwriting either a cap-rate compression or a take-private, neither of which is a base-case cash flow. HISTORY: operating EPS is flat over ten years (13.0c FY16 -> 12.9c FY26) despite ~25-30% retention, the FY20 equity raise (3,710m -> 3,933m securities) and rising debt costs (average borrowing rate 5.7% at June 2026, up from 5.4%); the base terminal growth of 2.5% therefore assumes the restocked development pipeline and 5.3% like-for-like rent growth do better than the last decade, and the bear case assumes they do not.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY27 guidance: operating EPS 13.2-13.4c vs 12.9c FY26 (midpoint +3.1%), FY26 AR line 2518
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-3.9% 3yr, -2.5% 5yr, driven by FY23-FY24 property devaluations) and operating EPS CAGR (-4.3% 3yr) diverge by >30% from revenue CAGR (+11.4% 3yr, +7.8% 5yr). Revenue growth is residential settlement volume (development revenue 1,895 of 2,654) and does not translate into earnings: operating profit fell from 580 (FY23) to 508 (FY26) over the same period on compressed development margins and higher interest costs. Neither CAGR is a forward anchor; guidance is.
historical_growth.notes: EPS and FCF CAGRs are computed on OPERATING EPS (14.7c FY23 / 13.97c FY21 -> 12.9c FY26) and Operating profit after tax (580 FY23 / 550 FY21 -> 508 FY26), Mirvac's distributable-earnings series. Statutory EPS is negative in FY23-FY24 and statutory FCF swings -796 to +571 on inventory timing, so neither supports a CAGR. Ten-year operating EPS CAGR (FY16 13.0c -> FY26 12.9c) is -0.1%.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 = guidance midpoint 13.3c (+3.1%) reproduced by 3% revenue growth at a flat 23.4% post-interest margin (operating profit ~523 = 13.2c). FY28 +4% as the guided step-up to 2,800-3,100 lot settlements (vs 2,130 FY26) and the 55 Pitt Street / Harbourside / Aspect completions flow through, then a fade to 2.5% by FY32: like-for-like rent growth (5.3% FY26) drifting back to CPI, development margins held at the low end of the 18-22% target band, and no further capital-partner sell-down gains assumed beyond the pipeline already secured.
base.margin_rationale: Post-net-interest EBITDA margin on operating revenue: FY26 actual 23.4%, FY25 23.2%. Held flat: the guided FY27 weighted average cost of debt of 5.7% is already the June 2026 rate, so no further interest-cost drag; no margin recovery credited either, because development margins are still below the 18-22% target and office expenses run ahead of rent.
base.capex_rationale: D&A add-back (2.4% of revenue) plus retained earnings reinvested (4.8%): operating profit 523 less distributions at the guided 9.9c (391) = 132 retained in FY27, a 75% payout consistent with FY26 (74%) and FY25 (75%). Held flat so retention stays ~25% of operating profit; at 2.5% terminal growth that requires a ~10% incremental return on retained equity, i.e. development returns at target rather than the 5.4% operating ROE on the whole book.

bull.growth_rationale: Top of guidance in FY27 (13.4c), then the restocked residential pipeline (three masterplanned communities launched in 4Q26, A$1.5bn pre-sales, Australian housing undersupply) delivers 3,100+ settlements a year at target margins, LIV build-to-rent stabilises above 95% and the ART partnership scales the funds platform; RBA easing takes the average borrowing rate from 5.7% toward 5.0% by FY29.
bull.margin_rationale: Each 50bp off the ~A$3.5bn net debt is ~A$18m of operating profit, ~0.6pp of margin; a 70bp rate fall plus development margins back inside the 18-22% band adds ~1.6pp by FY31.

bear.growth_rationale: FY27 lands at the bottom of guidance as settlements slip, then a FY25-style trough: residential margins compress and apartment settlements defer, office revaluations resume and look-through gearing (27.2%) drifts toward the 30% ceiling, forcing asset sales at soft prices and a dividend held at 9.9c; operating profit falls to ~A$430m (FY25 was 474) before recovering at the last decade's flat-to-2% per-security trend.
bear.margin_rationale: Rates stay at or above 5.7% as hedges (66%) roll off, development margins fall toward the low teens on cost inflation and delayed settlements, and unallocated overheads are not cut.

scenario_narratives.base: Mirvac earns its FY27 guidance (13.2-13.4c, DPS 9.9c) on 2,800-3,100 lot settlements and a 5.7% cost of debt, grows operating profit ~3-4% a year through FY29 as the secured commercial and mixed-use pipeline (55 Pitt Street, Harbourside, Aspect, SEED) completes, and then compounds at ~2.5% -- CPI-like rent growth on a 98%-occupied portfolio with a 75% payout. The A$3.5bn net debt is serviced inside the flows; no NTA convergence is assumed.
scenario_narratives.bull: Australian housing undersupply plus a restocked masterplanned-communities pipeline lifts settlements past 3,100 a year at 18-22% margins; RBA easing takes the average borrowing rate toward 5%; LIV build-to-rent and the ART-backed funds platform become a capital-light earnings leg. Operating EPS compounds ~5% a year to FY31 and the stock re-rates toward NTA (A$2.33).
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY23-FY25 pattern repeats: office values fall again, development margins stay compressed as settlements defer, look-through gearing approaches 30% and Mirvac recycles assets at soft prices or raises equity as in FY20. Operating profit troughs near A$430m in FY28 and per-security earnings resume the last decade's flat trend, so the distribution barely grows from 9.9c.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: a devaluation-driven statutory loss occurred in two of the last four years, look-through gearing (27.2%) sits in the upper half of the 20-30% target band, 34% of debt is unhedged at a 5.7% average rate, ~30% of operating EBIT is development profit that depends on settlement timing, and per-security operating earnings have not grown in ten years. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs rates, residential margins, office valuations and BTR occupancy to improve together, and FY27 guidance itself is only +3%. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Stapled REIT/developer valued on its own distributable measure (Operating profit after tax) as free cash flow to equity at a 9.5% AUD cost of equity, with reinvestment of the ~25% retained charged explicitly and net debt held at zero because the flow is post-interest. Statutory profit and statutory FCF are fair-value and inventory-timing noise and are ignored. The earnings-based value sits below NTA (A$2.33) because operating ROE on book (5.4%) is below the cost of equity; the current 24% discount to NTA is the market pricing the same gap.
key_risks_to_valuation: Interest rates: ~A$3.5bn net debt at 5.7% with 66% hedged; each 50bp is ~A$18m (3.5%) of operating profit.
Development cycle: A$1.9bn of development revenue and 270 of 908 segment EBIT depend on residential settlement timing and margins that are still below the 18-22% target band.
Office valuations: a further devaluation cycle would push look-through gearing toward the 30% ceiling and could force asset sales or an FY20-style equity raise (3,710m -> 3,933m securities).
Capital-partner dependence: FY26 operating profit included sell-down gains at Harbourside, SEED and Kindira; the base case assumes the secured pipeline continues to attract partners.
Ten-year record: operating EPS 13.0c (FY16) -> 12.9c (FY26) despite 25-30% retention; the 2.5% terminal growth assumes better capital allocation than the last decade delivered.
